Hi Laura — thanks for the examples. I'm Marissa on Billing & Pricing; copying Karthik for the runtime specifics. Below is the official phrasing we use in contracts and the way the hosted API is billed today. I'll include a worked example that matches your CSV rows.

Official policy (hosted API):
- Input tokens: tokens that are part of the request payload sent to the model. This includes system messages, all message role tokens (user/assistant/system), and any tokens in tool/function call *arguments* that you send to the runtime.
- Output tokens: tokens that are generated by the model and returned to the caller, including tool/function responses returned to the chat. If your runtime calls an external tool and the tool returns text that we then forward back in the API response, that text is billed as output tokens.
- Streaming & partial generations: billing is calculated on the full tokenized content actually transmitted/returned to you. If you stream n tokens and then stop the stream, you are charged for the n tokens returned.
- Rounding: we apply a per-request rounding model. For each API request we calculate exact token counts (input and output) and then round up the sum to the next whole token — there is no coarser bucketing. We do not aggregate rounding across multiple requests or across a billing period; rounding happens at the request granularity.
- Caching/Prefix reuse: automatic prefix/KV caching reduces compute but does not alter how tokens are counted on the invoice — you are still billed for the logical token counts in the request/response. The exception is when a request is satisfied entirely from an internal cache without invoking the model; in that case 0 model tokens are billed (but cache-hit behavior is only available on select Dedicated/private deployments today).

Worked example (matches row 1 in your CSV):
- System prompt: 20 tokens (input)
- User message: 150 tokens (input)
- Model generates a function call (no output text) and returns a function response of 80 tokens (output)
Billing math per request:
- Input tokens = 20 + 150 = 170
- Output tokens = 80
- Total billed tokens for the request = 170 (input) + 80 (output) = 250 tokens
- Rounding: we already measure in integer tokens; per-request rounding is to the next whole token — in this example there's no fractional token, so billed = 250 tokens.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- Tool calls that return structured JSON: we tokenize the returned text representation that is sent back in the API response and bill on those output tokens. If you post-process tool responses client-side (i.e., tool returns binary or a reference and you don't return a textual body), only the text actually returned to the API caller is counted.
- System tokens injected by Redwood (for safety or routing) are included in input counts when they are part of the API payload. If you use the "system" role in the chat messages you send, those tokens count towards input.
- If a single user request triggers multiple model calls under the hood (e.g., internal re-ranking or reruns for safety), we bill for the sum of model calls that were executed on behalf of your API request. We surface re-runs in the Console trace and in the per-route token breakdown.
